You have 60 calendar days from the date of this notice to request an Internal Appeal. However, if you are now receiving these services, and you want these services to continue automatically during the appeal, you must either request an Internal Appeal on or before the final day of the previously approved authorization, or request an Intemal Appeal within 10 calendar days of the date of this notice, whichever is later.  If you do not request your appeal within these timeframes, the services will not continue during the appeal. Horizon NJ Health will decide your Internal Appeal within 30 calendar days of receipt of your appeal.  If you or your treating provider believe this 30 calendar-day timeframe for deciding your appeal is too long and could harm your health, please call Horizon NJ Health at 1-800-682-9094 x89606 (TTY 711) and ask for an expedited, or fast, appeal. An expedited or fast appeal means that we will decide your Internal Appeal within 72 hours of receipt. You may ask for an expedited, or fast, appeal if you are an inpatient in a facility, if the care you received was for an urgent or emergency health concern, or if it is medically necessary and taking 30 calendar days to decide the appeal could seriously harm you in some way.

We will give you a decision within 36 hours after receipt of your request if your plan provides two levels of appeal or 72 hours after receipt of your request if your plan provides one level of appeal. If your appeal is about your continued stay in a facility to treat a substance use disorder and you have not been discharged, we'll give you a decision within 24 hours after receipt of your request. You may also request an expedited external review at the same time as your expedited Stage 1 appeal.  For all other Stage 1 appeals, we will give you a decision within 10 calendar days after receipt of your request.  As part of a Stage 1 appeal of a denial based on medical necessity, you (or your provider with your consent) may also ask to speak with the Medical Director who made the initial coverage denial.  Stage 2 appeal  If you do not agree with the Stage 1 appeal decision, you may request a Stage 2 appeal if your plan provides a second level of appeal, or you may be able to request an external review if your plan does not provide a second level of appeal. Your Stage 1 appeal decision letter will tell you what additional appeal rights you may have.  External review  If your appeal results in our continued denial of payment or coverage based on medical necessity, or we do not give you a timely appeal decision, you can request an external review of your claim by an independent third party, who will review the denial and issue a final decision.
